title: Sell Mineral Rights in Masontown, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Masontown, PA | Fayette County
metaDescription: Masontown, PA mineral owners: we buy Fayette County Marcellus and legacy interests directly along the Monongahela, with a plain-language division order review.
heroLead: Masontown grew up on coal along the Monongahela River, and a lot of the mineral rights under Fayette County land carry that same layered history — coal severed one generation, gas leased another.
intro: If your family has owned ground around Masontown for a few generations, there's a real chance your deed already shows a severed coal estate from the old German-Masontown Coke Company days, with oil and gas rights handled separately, sometimes by a different owner entirely. That layering is exactly why Fayette County mineral titles take more care to read than a one-page lease summary suggests.

We buy Marcellus interests and legacy oil and gas rights around Masontown directly. We're not brokers shopping your interest to someone else; we review the title ourselves, tell you what we find, and make an offer based on it.

sections.heading: Coal, Coke, and Gas Under the Same Ground
paragraphs: Fayette County's coal history runs deep, and the coke ovens that once lined the Monongahela near Masontown left behind a pattern of severed mineral estates that still shapes title work today. In some cases the coal was sold off outright while oil and gas stayed with the surface owner's heirs, which is good news if that's your situation, since it means your gas rights weren't caught up in the coal transaction at all.

The Marcellus wet-gas window reaches into this part of Fayette County, and operators have leased and pooled tracts around Masontown and neighboring German Township over the past decade. If you signed a lease yourself, or inherited one, we'll look at the bonus terms and royalty clause together with you.

sections.heading: Reading Your Fayette County Deed History
paragraphs: We pull records from the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown to trace how your interest was created, whether by a reservation clause when a family farm sold, or by direct inheritance from a relative who never sold the surface at all.

Masontown deeds from the early-to-mid 1900s sometimes use language that's hard to interpret without doing this kind of research, so we do the digging rather than asking you to guess what your grandparent's lawyer meant sixty years ago.

sections.heading: What Your Royalty Check Isn't Telling You
paragraphs: Post-production deduction disputes have shaped Pennsylvania royalty law for years, and a lot of older Fayette County leases were written before the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act set a one-eighth floor. If your check shows gathering and compression fees stripped out before your percentage is applied, that's a lease-language issue, not something you did wrong.
We'll go through your actual statements with you, in plain terms, before we ever talk numbers.

faqs.question: My deed mentions a severed coal estate. Does that affect my gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Coal, oil, and gas are frequently severed separately in Fayette County, so a coal reservation from a hundred years ago doesn't automatically mean your oil and gas interest went with it. We'll trace that specifically for your parcel.

faqs.question: Is my interest too small to matter if it's split among cousins?
faqs.answer: Fractional interests split among heirs are the norm around Masontown, not the exception. We regularly buy interests that are a fraction of a fraction, as long as the title traces cleanly.

faqs.question: Do you handle the Recorder of Deeds paperwork?
faqs.answer: Yes. Once we agree on terms, we prepare and record the transfer documents with the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds so you don't have to manage that process yourself.
